WAR DEPARDMEYE
HEADQUART RS NINTH CORPS AREA
OFFICE OF THE AIR OFFICER
Presidio of San Francisco, Calit.
October 6th, 1925.
Excerpt from lst Lieut.
H. A. Moore's letter.
"In reply to your letter of September 15th to Colonel F. P. Lahm, who is
at present away from the City on a short leave of absence, I am enclosing herewith
the sketch which you requested, together with some additional information on
landing field requirements and an estimate of costs.
As the field stands to-day, the runways - as I have placed them - are
entirely too short to accommodate all types of planes. If you want to go into
this matter in the right way, the thing to do is to extend the runways on out
into the marshy ground - making them appriximately fifty yaras wide and as far
Northeast and Southeast as possible, bearing in mind the high power lines and
the fact
that an obstacle at the edge of a field cuts off seven feet of runway
for each obstacle of its own height. Perhaps three or four hundred feet could
be added in this way. According to the chart, the prevailing winds will pernit
of landing into the Northwest and Southwest.
As the field is too smell for a
runway from East to West, I have placed the hangars, shops, etcetera, along the
West edge of the field next to the highway.
The entire portion of hard ground
must be dragged and smoothed before being used.
I vould like to suggest that if you care to look into the future, when you
need a much larger airport, you might consider the proposition of having the
P. G. & E. power lines removed and filling in the marshland to the Bast, thereby
providing a field with a one-half mile runway Best and West.
In such eyent the
hangars could be located on the North and South side of the field. You would
then have a sufficient area for every type of plane, together with a high
factor of safety.
Any telephone, telegraph, or power line around a field is a
potential menaceto landing and taking off."
